name_reason: Conforms to fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> (domain=ani_decoder/animation). Descriptor 'sparse_copy_literal' accurately captures behavior: sparse=offset-addressed segments, copy=memcpy of stream bytes, literal=raw uncompressed bytes. Parallels well-formed siblings fd2_ani_decoder_chunk_sparse_set_byte / sparse_set_run_byte. No Ghidra address residue.
purpose: ANI delta-stream chunk handler: applies N sparse literal-copy segments {offset, length, literal bytes} into the current row destination buffer (each segment memcpy'd to dst_buf + offset).
logic_summary: Reads ushort N = segment count, then loops N times. Each iteration: reads ushort offset, byte length, then memcpy's 'length' literal bytes from the stream cursor to dst_buf + offset. In the binary the copy is the Watcom inlined memcpy idiom (SHR ECX,1; REP MOVSW; RCL ECX,1; REP MOVSB = word copy + odd-byte tail). dst pointer is reset from EBX (=dst_buf base) each iteration; the cursor advances by 2 + sum_i(3 + length_i). No return value.

returns.semantics: none (writes decoded literal bytes into the row destination buffer; advances the shared stream cursor)

reads_globals: g_ani_cursor (file-static stream cursor; C analog of the binary's ESI)
writes_globals: g_ani_cursor (file-static stream cursor advanced past the consumed segments)
notes: Disasm (LODSW count; per-segment LODSW offset / LODSB length / REP MOVSW+MOVSB copy; DEC EDX loop) and decompilation both match the C source at anidec.c lines 277-295 exactly; faithful equivalence-preserving translation. Invoked indirectly via dispatch table slot @ 0x5278E (frame dispatch table @ 0x5276A), so get_function_callers reports none and the only xref is DATA from 0x5278E -- expected. Binary uses ESI as the stream cursor; the C version uses file-static g_ani_cursor (documented at anidec.c header lines 6-8), an intentional translation, not a logic change. Live Ghidra signature is __watcall void(void). No edit needed: name keep, comment keep, plate consistent with src so left untouched.
